note.text: Family-life discussions can examine cooperation, communication and differing responsibilities. Avoid claiming that every household has the same members or arrangements. Give reasons, listen to another view and distinguish a suggestion from a command. Learners can use fictional households and are not required to share private events. A disagreement should address the action or proposal rather than a person’s worth. Respectful language can still express a clear limit or seek help.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to exchange views about shared responsibilities, respect and communication using fictional situations. Builds on: polite offers, directed purpose and careful word choice. Leads to: reading an original family-life passage and writing to different audiences.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original dialogue: In a fictional household, study time overlaps with chores. Bih proposes discussing the fixed deadlines. Ayuk says a fair plan must consider each person’s responsibilities and available time. They agree to ask a responsible adult to help adjust the arrangement. The exchange offers a possible process, not a judgment that every household must follow one schedule.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Prepare short turns: state the point, give a relevant reason and invite a response. Use fictional people if the subject is private. Practise with a partner when available; written choices here do not establish oral fluency or listening ability. Challenge an idea without insulting the speaker.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Fairness always means identical tasks for every person regardless of circumstances. Correction: Responsibilities should be considered with the actual circumstances.
A suggestion needs no connection to the stated difficulty. Correction: A useful proposal responds to the actual problem.
Listening means preparing an insult before the other person finishes. Correction: Understand the point before answering it.
Class participation requires private family disclosure. Correction: Fictional examples allow participation while respecting privacy.
